items.title: Regression - 1.34 Insiders tries to open non-existent files in /.vscode folder

labels.name: config
labels.description: VS Code configuration, settings

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Remote system operations issues

items.body:
A FileSystemProvider extension that provides a /.vscode folder containing only a settings.json file also gets asked by 1.34.0-insider to readFile non-existent files named tasks.json and launch.json from that folder. This does not happen on 1.33.1

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Obtain the MemFS sample (git clone https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode-extension-samples and then go to the fsprovider-sample subdir)
2. In src/extension.ts add the following lines to the function that is registered as implementing the 'memfs.init' command [(code pointer)](https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode-extension-samples/blob/c3f551e86c1de21ac26afad2886b2e40df7f1f9d/fsprovider-sample/src/extension.ts#L39)
```
        // canary .vscode folder with stub settings.json file
        memFs.createDirectory(vscode.Uri.parse(`memfs:/.vscode/`));
        memFs.writeFile(vscode.Uri.parse(`memfs:/.vscode/settings.json`), Buffer.from('{\n}'), { create: true, overwrite: true });
```
3. At the start of the `stat` method of the `MemFS` class in src/fileSystemProvider.ts [(code pointer)](https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode-extension-samples/blob/c3f551e86c1de21ac26afad2886b2e40df7f1f9d/fsprovider-sample/src/fileSystemProvider.ts#L59) add a logpoint with the following message: `stat {uri.path}`
4. At the start of the `readFile` method [(code pointer)](https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode-extension-samples/blob/c3f551e86c1de21ac26afad2886b2e40df7f1f9d/fsprovider-sample/src/fileSystemProvider.ts#L74) add a logpoint with the following message: `readFile {uri.path}`
5. Launch debugging using the 'Launch Extension' configuration.
6. When the [Extension Development Host] window appears, switch to it and run (e.g. F1) the command `MemFS: Setup Workspace` followed by the command `MemFS: Create Files`

Debug Console output from 1.34.0-insider is:
```
MemFS says "Hello"
MemFS says "Hello"
readFile /.vscode/settings.json
readFile /.vscode/tasks.json
readFile /.vscode/launch.json
readFile /.vscode/settings.json
readFile /.vscode/tasks.json
readFile /.vscode/launch.json
stat /.vscode/settings.json
stat /.vscode/tasks.json
stat /.vscode/launch.json
stat /.vscode/settings.json
stat /.vscode/tasks.json
stat /.vscode/launch.json
stat /.vscode/tasks.json
stat /.vscode/launch.json
stat /.vscode/tasks.json
stat /.vscode/launch.json
```

Using 1.33.1 the same procedure gives:
```
MemFS says "Hello"
MemFS says "Hello"
stat /.vscode
stat /.vscode/settings.json
readFile /.vscode/settings.json
```

Notice how 1.33.1 stats the .vscode folder and its settings.json file before reading the file, whereas 1.34-insider reads that file (twice) **and** attempts to read the non-existent files tasks.json and launch.json (again, twice), only issuing stat calls on the files afterwards.


VS Code version: Code - Insiders 1.34.0-insider (0fde6619172c9f04c41f2e816479e432cc974b8b, 2019-04-25T05:24:52.804Z)
OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.16299

before the most recent update, I could start ipython in the integrated terminal, copy several lines of code from the editor window, and paste them into ipython as a single code cell. After the update, now pasting a selection of more than 2 lines into ipython in the integrated terminal puts each line in its own ipython cell (which obviously doesn't work for pasting in loops or function definitions) and yields the much-discussed `IndentationError`. - VSCode Version: 1.51.0-insider, commit 605bc4ec
- OS Version: Win10 10.0.19042.508

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the latest Docker extension [nightly build](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docker/issues/1408), or at least 1.7.0
1. Create a Node express app in a subfolder and open the parent folder in VSCode
1. Add Dockerfiles to workspace, Node.js, etc.
1. Right click the Dockerfile in the subfolder and click "Build Image"

Expected:
The `docker-build` task in .vscode/tasks.json executes

Actual:
Nothing happens, but I see this error if I'm debugging the Docker extension in the outer VSCode window:
```
rejected promise not handled within 1 second: TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'name' of '(intermediate value)' as it is null.
 extensionHostProcess.js
stack trace: TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'name' of '(intermediate value)' as it is null.
	at Object.findPreferredPM (c:\Users\bwater\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\resources\app\extensions\npm\dist\npmMain.js:14:49429)
	at async v (c:\Users\bwater\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\resources\app\extensions\npm\dist\npmMain.js:1:12156)
	at async A (c:\Users\bwater\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\resources\app\extensions\npm\dist\npmMain.js:1:14173)
	at async E (c:\Users\bwater\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\resources\app\extensions\npm\dist\npmMain.js:1:13606)
	at async c:\Users\bwater\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\resources\app\extensions\npm\dist\npmMain.js:1:12604
	at async y (c:\Users\bwater\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\resources\app\extensions\npm\dist\npmMain.js:1:12310)
 extensionHostProcess.js
```

I think this is a regression due to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f8c0e3b612733b1f78d354556e8767a85f50ab87. When I change the setting `npm.packageManager` to `npm`, the issue goes away. I can then change it back to `auto` and it stays gone. However, if I restart VSCode with `auto` the issue returns.

My guess is that `which-pm` is returning null because it does not find anything in the root workspace folder (the express app is in a subfolder), and then [this](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f8c0e3b612733b1f78d354556e8767a85f50ab87/extensions/npm/src/preferred-pm.ts#L68) line fails to destructure.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17436829/99582473-d2c2cd00-29ea-11eb-8751-a07f33f3fdcc.png)


<!-- Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes**

Strange thing is, I only noticed this after update to 1.51.1 (from 1.48.2). I tried reinstalling 1.48.2 only to find out that it has exact same behaviour. I then tried 1.45.1 and it was back to how I used to.

Event stranger thing is that I have another laptop (**Windows 10 1909**) with 1.48.2 installed and shift+alt+o would organize imports into **single line**. I then updated to 1.51.1 and it would still do **single line organize**.

I am not sure what is going on, but I asked a few colleagues about this and they too noticed that after recent update imports are not organized into single line.

All behaviours were observed with and without extensions.
